records.text: Misha is a beast who can roar loudly and rake her claws against the gronn's altar.
Anger Guards are combat creatures; they cast a spell while in combat.
Expedition Wardens enforce conduct on neutral ground, threatening intruders and invoking the blade when confronting an opponent. Their lines are disciplinary and hostile.

Kialon Nightblade is Timothy’s associate in Sylvanaar. Timothy sends him a private response, and Kialon laughs at Timothy’s claim to have matters under control, noting that he has not changed and corrected Kialon’s spelling. Kialon sighs at having sent the letter, expecting Timothy to manage the situation himself as usual.

Nekthar is concerned about the ogre threat to Zabra’jin and says Thunderlord Stronghold has troubles of its own. He can share what his people know of the local ogre tribes and their tactics, while reinforcements are limited.
Morcrush is a formidable combatant whose tactics include a close-range War Stomp and summoning Morcrush Shardlings as his health falls.
Hemathion is a combatant whose attacks include Flame Breath and a Terrifying Roar.

Speaker Mar’grom calls for unity among the Ogre clans, warning that division will bring their destruction. He rejects Mog’dorg’s proposed rule as replacing the gronn overlords with another master, and resists both gronn rule and outsiders who threaten the clans.
Amerun Leafshade is a hippogryph master who offers a flight service and asks where a traveler would like to fly. If attacked, he calls for guards and summons an enraged hippogryph.
Unoke Tenderhoof is a wind rider master offering fast travel. If attacked, he calls for guards and summons an enraged wyvern.
A Thunderlord Grunt is a rank-and-file fighter identified by the Thunderlord name.
Pol Snowhoof is a trade goods vendor who offers goods for browsing.

Gholah is an innkeeper who welcomes battle-weary visitors to rest by the fire and share stories. He speaks of making these new lands home, and Gholah also offers goods and a seasonal trick-or-treat interaction.

Old Orok sells fruit and fungus and supplies preserved fruit for Rocket-Chief Fuselage's order. Orok admits not understanding the technical specifications, but says the price is right; Orok directs the buyer to deliver the crate in Area 52.
Threlc is a fishmonger whose goods are available to browse.
Raiza specializes in throwing weapons and ammunition, and also offers goods and equipment repairs.
Karnaze is a general goods merchant, offering wares for customers to browse.
Lor is a stable master associated with pet stabling and help recovering lost companions.
Fera Palerunner is a First Aid trainer. She points trainees seeking further advancement to Doctor Gregory Victor in Hammerfall.
Orgatha is a named axesmith who sells goods and provides repairs.

Innkeeper Shaunessy is presented as an innkeeper who invites weary visitors to rest beneath the inn's roof and invokes Elune in a greeting. Visitors can make the inn home, browse goods, and ask for a seasonal Trick or Treat interaction.
Caoileann is a named trade-goods vendor.
Tanaide is a named general-goods vendor.
Cahill is a named weaponsmith who sells goods and provides repairs.
A sentinel of Sylvanaar.

Baelmon the Hound-Master is an elite demon who speaks for the Burning Legion. His recorded lines direct an arriving ally through the materialization chamber toward Forge Camp Wrath, while his combat taunts threaten torture and death.
Daga Ramba is identified as a potions seller, with a vendor interaction for browsing goods.
Steamwheedle Sam is an arena organizer. He also offers information about forming a guild.
Meminnie is identified as an arena vendor.
“Lefty” Puddemup is an arena battlemaster for the Steamwheedle Fighting Circuit. He brusquely dismisses one prospective challenger and questions another about joining the arena battlegrounds.
Lashh'an Talonite is a Lashh'an combatant. It uses Backstab in combat.
A Lashh'an Wing Guard is a combatant that makes a break for the nearest rune circle; it also uses Debilitating Strike in combat.
A Lashh'an Windwalker is a combatant that casts spells in battle, including when a fight begins.
A Bloodmaul Skirmisher is a blunt, aggressive fighter. It threatens to smash its opponents in short, broken phrases, whether it is angry or simply roused to fight.

A Bloodmaul Geomancer is a blunt combatant whose threats center on smashing or crushing its opponent. Unlike the Skirmisher's repeated boasts about smashing, the Geomancer also threatens simply, “I'll crush you!”
A Bloodmaul Lookout serves as a sentry, a watchful role among the Bloodmaul forces.
A Bloodmaul Brewmaster is a blunt, threatening fighter, using the same smashing taunts heard from Bloodmaul Skirmishers and Geomancers.
Doomforge Engineers are hostile engineers in the Deathforge area of Shadowmoon Valley. They attack with a spell when combat begins.
Doomforge Attendants are hostile inhabitants of the Deathforge area in Shadowmoon Valley. They use a spell as they become badly wounded.
Abyssal Flamebringers are demons found in Shadowmoon Valley's Deathforge area. Banishment can alter their behavior, and their deaths can trigger credit for Banish the Demons.
Deathforge Over-Smiths are hostile figures in the Deathforge. In combat, they use Slime Spray and Toxic Slime.
Deathforge Technicians are hostile figures found at several sites around the Deathforge. In combat, they can use Steal Armor.
Void Terrors are hostile creatures encountered at the Deathforge. They use a spell in combat.
Vekh'nir Keeneye is a beast. It casts an ability while it fights.
Vekh'nir Stormcaller is a beast. It casts abilities while it fights.
Vekh'nir Dreadhawk is a beast. It casts an ability while it fights.
Ruuan'ok Cloudgazer is a beast. It casts an ability while it fights.
Ruuan'ok Skyfury is a beast. It casts an ability during combat.
Ruuan'ok Ravenguard is a humanoid combatant whose fighting routine includes casting a spell.
Grishna Falconwing is a Grishna humanoid encountered in the Blade’s Edge region. It casts Bestial Wrath in combat, and its death triggers Understanding Ravenspeech.
Grishna Harbinger is a Grishna humanoid whose combat ability is Shriveling Gaze.
Grishna Scorncrow is a Grishna humanoid encountered in the Blade’s Edge region. It casts Gushing Wound in combat, and its death triggers Understanding Ravenspeech.
A Bloodmaul Brute is one of the Bloodmaul ogres targeted around Bloodmaul Outpost. It meets intruders with blunt threats to smash them.
The Bloodmaul Shaman is a shaman. Its combat calls threaten to smash or crush its opponent, matching the aggressive posture shown by the Bloodmaul group.
A Bloodmaul Mauler is among the ogres Tor’chunk urges the player to attack at Bloodmaul Camp. Its aggro calls threaten to smash an opponent, with one variant declaring anger.

A Bloodmaul warlock of the ogre clan, found around Bloodmaul Camp and the nearby mountains. Tor'chunk's campaign treats the warlocks as part of the camp's force, though his request to kill them belongs to him, not to each warlock. This warlock prepares Demon Armor and meets intruders with blunt threats to smash or crush them.

A Bladespire ogre brute among the clan's forces at Bladespire Hold and the surrounding grounds. Brutes answer intruders with threats and insults, and this one uses Cleave in combat. Tor'chunk identifies the Bladespire as a powerful clan favored by Gruul and his sons; his call to kill them is his campaign, not this brute's personal account.

A Bladespire battlemage stationed among the tough ogres guarding the exterior of Gruul's Lair. It attacks with the clan's blunt threats, and a conditional death line says it is going to Ogri'la. Tor'chunk names battlemages among the lair's defenders, but the quest's account of Gruul's protection is his own framing.

A Bladespire enforcer among the tough ogres guarding Gruul's Lair. Enforcers are named among the targets at the lair's exterior, where Tor'chunk says Gruul keeps his strongest ogres. This enforcer greets intruders with insults and threats to smash them; those lines portray its immediate hostility, not a broader personal motive.
A Bladespire shaman of the ogre clan, found among its forces in the Bladespire Grounds and nearby mountain areas. Its combat lines are blunt threats to smash or crush intruders.

A Bloodmaul dire wolf serving as a sentry in the ogres' nearby pack. Rina's Horde-side effort to find replacement wolves leads her to ask that these wolves be diminished with her fey-drake dust, rather than killed.

Grimnok Battleborn is an ogre leader at Southmaul Tower who ordered a march on Bladespire Hold and coveted Gorr'Dim's head as a trophy. He speaks in blunt, broken phrases, boasts of smashing opponents, and wants Alliance and Horde intruders dead. T'chali accuses him of leading the party that buried him and left him to die; Grimnok's own lines do not confirm that account. In death, he wonders whether Ogri'la exists and says he feels honored to be killed by a king or queen.
A Lashh'an matriarch in Blade's Edge Mountains.
An Ancient Protector associated with Sylvanaar in Blade's Edge Mountains.
A tame Kaliri found in Blade's Edge Mountains.
A Vekh'nir matriarch in Blade's Edge Mountains.
A Ruuan'ok matriarch in Blade's Edge Mountains.
An Arakkoa egg found in Blade's Edge Mountains. On respawn, and when a creature with line of sight comes within six yards, it casts the Arakkoa Egg Debuff on itself.

Grulloc is a gronn known as the son of Gruul. He speaks in a blunt, simple manner, boasts about keeping a pig as a pet, and says he enjoys chasing it and eating bacon. His words make him sound easily entertained and focused on food.
Cymbre Starsong is a general goods vendor in Blade's Edge. Visitors can browse her goods.
Rashere Pridehoof is a trade goods vendor in Blade's Edge. Visitors can browse his goods.
The Grishna Matriarch is a creature found in Blade's Edge.
The Bloodmaul Battle Worg is a trained battle animal found in Blade's Edge. It can detect stealth.
The Bladespire Cook is an aggressive cook whose threats promise to smash intruders. Its combat barks use blunt, broken phrasing, including a threat to smash its target in the face.
A searing elemental found in the Blade's Edge Mountains.
Wrath Hounds are beasts encountered in Blade's Edge Mountains.
Maggoc is identified as the Son of Gruul. He is a singular, powerful creature in Blade's Edge Mountains, and his combat routine includes Mortal Wound and Rock Rumble.
Razaani Raiders are combatants encountered in Blade's Edge Mountains. This raider uses Energy Flare in combat.
Razaani Nexus Stalkers are combatants encountered in Blade's Edge Mountains. This stalker uses Intangible Presence in combat.
A Razaani spell-thief of Blade's Edge, this combatant unleashes an energy surge in battle. Its death triggers the summoning of a Deadsoul Orb.
A Razaani light orb found in Blade's Edge. It reacts when struck by Magnetic Pull, marking it as part of the area's magical activity.
A fiendling flesh beast found north of Razor Ridge, where these creatures are studied. Its ether-energized flesh is collected as a study specimen.
A Fey Drake of Blade's Edge, it enters combat with Mana Burn and can blink during battle.

Ridgespine Stalkers are stealthy spiders that live among the rock outcroppings of Razor Ridge and Scalewing Shelf. Their ambushes threaten passersby and the nearby Roughriders' efforts to keep those routes clear.

Korgaah is a Bladespire leader at the north end of Bladespire Hold, where sober defenders guard him. T'chali accuses Korgaah of raiding south and kicking him while he lay wounded; that account makes Korgaah a target of T'chali's revenge. Korgaah fights with spells.

Mugdorg is one of the Bladespire leaders at Bladespire Hold and is said to carry Vindicator Vuuleen's shield. Vuuleen is gathering information on the Bladespire while remaining in her cage, and identifies Mugdorg as one of the leaders who took her belongings. Sober guards protect him.

Bladespire Raptors inhabit Bladespire Hold and the surrounding grounds alongside the Bladespire ogres. Their presence contributes to the threat facing Thunderlord Stronghold; they attack with a distinctive combat ability.
A Bladespire Ravager is a beast serving among the clan’s hardiest fighters around Gruul’s lair. It attacks intruders and is counted among the targets in the assault on the lair.
Glumdor is a Bladespire ogre who tries to seize an opponent’s weapon and threatens to crush them. He fights with Cutdown.

Droggam is a Bladespire leader who carries Vindicator Vuuleen’s sword. Vuuleen is gathering information on the clan while held in a cage, and identifies Droggam as one of the two leaders holding her belongings.

Gorr'Dim leads the Bladespire Hold ogres, whose dominance in the mountains has made them favored by Gruul. He keeps an entourage that includes defenders who refuse the Bloodmaul brew; Sylvanaar’s representative calls him crafty and warns against underestimating him.
The Silkwing Larva is a creature that can metamorphose as it is wounded; its change is announced during combat.

A Thunderlord dire wolf found in the Ruuan Weald and Blade's Edge areas. It is a hostile animal involved in the local effort to protect the area: striking one with Gor’drek’s ointment advances the objective “Protecting Our Own.”
A Scalewing serpent inhabiting the Ruuan Weald and nearby Blade’s Edge areas. It is a hostile creature that uses Lightning Strike in combat, one of the dangers encountered in the region.
Daggermaw Lashtails are creatures encountered in the Ruuan Weald and nearby Blade’s Edge areas. They are hostile combatants.
Dorgok is an ogre leader at Bloodmaul Camp, named as the target of a Sylvanaar objective concerning the Bloodmaul offensive.
A Bladespire chef encountered in Blade’s Edge Mountains. Though his title is that of a cook, he is an aggressive ogre: he threatens to smash whoever confronts him.

Fingrom is identified as a leader of the Bladespire ogres guarding the exterior of Gruul’s Lair. The objective against him is part of a campaign to weaken the clan; in combat, he uses Ice Barrier and Fireball.
A Bladespire crusher who dismisses opponents as puny and threatens to smash them in anger.
A Bladespire mystic who dismisses opponents as puny and threatens to smash them in anger.
Gnosh Brognat leads the ogres at Bladespire Outpost. Gnosh scorns opponents as puny and threatens to smash them; when facing death, Gnosh speaks of going to Ogri’la.
An Ethereum Prisoner (Group Energy Ball) in Blade's Edge Mountains.
Noko Moonwhisper is a reagent vendor in Blade’s Edge.
Xerintha Ravenoak is a food and drink vendor in Blade’s Edge.
Zinyen Swiftstrider is a weapon vendor who also repairs equipment. Travelers can browse his goods through the available vendor services.
Grishnath basilisks are found in the Blade’s Edge Mountains. This basilisk can feign death, then spring up and charge; it also uses Soften in combat.
Scalded basilisks range across parts of the Blade’s Edge Mountains. One may play dead before charging, and it uses Heat Wave in combat.
Ruuan Weald basilisks inhabit the Ruuan Weald. They can play dead before charging, and their combat behavior includes a Threshalisk Charge.
Ridgespine Horrors are found in Blade’s Edge Mountains. In combat, they use Web and Toxic Spit.
Lesser Nether Drakes are found in Blade’s Edge Mountains. They use a combat ability as their health falls into a low range.
A Scorch Imp is one of the Burning Legion's imps that burned Mosswood the Ancient's former home. The imps remain on the plateau northeast of him, where he asks for help making them afraid.

Grovestalker lynxes in the Living Grove have escaped Sylvanaar's control and begun encroaching on the settlement, causing unpleasant incidents. Sylvanaar's account suspects the arakkoa of Veil Lashh are behind the change, but identifies the lynxes as the immediate danger.

Stronglimb Deeproot is an ancient of war and chief defender of the Living Grove south of Sylvanaar. A wanted notice directs hunters across the bridge over Bloodmaul Ravine to find him and bring his hewn trunk to Tor'chunk Twoclaws.

Dreadwing is identified as the brood mother of the nether drakes infesting the crystals at Singing Ridge. Sylvanaar's scouting report says their numbers have grown enough to threaten the surrounding area and describes Dreadwing as an adult drake.

Bladewing Bloodletters are common, aggressive creatures of the Jagged Ridge. The Thunderlord at the stronghold describe them as a plague that eats and breeds incessantly, and seek to cull them; the bloodletters attack with poison and blood-leeching magic.
Outraged Raven's Wood Saplings are hostile plant creatures found across Raven's Wood. They remain dangerous when wounded, using a spell as their health falls.
Dire Ravens are dangerous wild birds of Raven's Wood. They use a spell when badly wounded.

Boulder'mok Brutes are Bladespire ogres at Boulder'mok. Tor'chunk Twoclaws calls for their destruction to keep the mountain ogres from overrunning the Thunderlord, and Brutes fight with a powerful attack.

Boulder'mok Shamans are Bladespire ogres stationed at Boulder'mok alongside the Brutes. Tor'chunk Twoclaws calls for the ogres' destruction to protect the Thunderlord; the Shamans answer an attack with magic.
The Boulder'mok Chieftain is an ogre at Boulder'mok. The chieftain uses a combat spell.

Rina Moonspring tends the Living Grove near Sylvanaar, using a nature-imbued bough to strengthen its treant defenses. She worries that the grove and Sylvanaar are exposed to threats, suspects the arakkoa may be behind the lynxes’ loss of control, and regards the grove’s health as essential to their safety.
A Mok'Nathal hunter.
Krugash is a Mok’Nathal general-goods vendor in the settlement.
Erool is a Mok’Nathal trade-goods vendor in the settlement.
Braagor is a butcher and sells goods.
Ragar is identified as a leatherworking-supplies vendor.
Ruka is identified with smashing weapons and offers weapon goods and repair service.
Grikka is a master leatherworking trainer.
Matron Varah is an innkeeper who asks for raptor ribs and serpent flesh. In return, she offers cooked dishes and recipes. She invites wanderers to rest by her fires and make the inn a home.
Spiritcaller Grakosh is a humanoid in Blade's Edge Mountains.
Spiritcaller Roxnak is a humanoid in Blade's Edge Mountains.
Spiritcaller Skrash is a humanoid in Blade's Edge Mountains.

Rip Pedalslam is a gryphon master eager to improve the Wildhammer dwarves’ mounts. Rip proposes adding an altimeter, rear-view mirror and rocket to create the TurboGryphon 8000, and asks a traveler to take these ideas to the roost keepers. When threatened, Rip calls for guards.

Fizit “Doc” Clocktock runs the Toshley’s Station inn and practices medicine. Doc hopes drake essences could cure many maladies and studies whether the nether mutation of black dragon eggs offers new benefits. Doc admits uncertainty about the temporal phase modulator’s effects and offers preliminary concoctions for testing.
Bembil Knockhammer sells general goods.

Bossi Pentapiston is a gnomish engineering supplier at Area 52. He says he rarely collaborates with goblins, yet agreed to help Rocket-Chief Fuselage by sending unused parts for his project, joking that fine gnomish parts might keep it from exploding.
Sassa Weldwell is a Trade Goods supplier at Area 52 who offers goods for browsing.
Station Technician is an Area 52 technician whose cries include “YEOW!!,” “I'M ON FIRE!!!,” and “IT BURNS!!”.
Station Guard is an Area 52 guard that uses a Tech Gun in combat.

Gor'drek is a Thunderlord shaman who honors the sacrifices of his ancestors and sees the clan's survival as a duty to future generations. At Thunderlord Stronghold, he directs efforts against threats to the clan, including bloodletters and Alliance defenses, and seeks to strengthen its dire wolves with magical ointment.

Razak Ironsides commands the defenders at Toshley's Station during ravager attacks. Blunt and energetic under pressure, he calls for reinforcements and orders the defenders to fire the defense guns. He seeks daggermaw teeth to make close-range weapons for his soldiers, measuring the work by whether it saves even one life.
The Felsworn Scalewing is one of the Felsworn creatures the Burning Legion sends against the land. It is found in Bladed Gulch, where the Felsworn are hunted among the forces spreading corruption.

The Felsworn Daggermaw is one of the Felsworn creatures the Burning Legion sends against the land. It is found around Bladed Gulch, where the Felsworn are hunted among the forces spreading corruption.

Tor'chunk Twoclaws is a hard-pressed defender of Thunderlord Stronghold, treating the nearby ogre clans as a grave threat and urging attacks on them. He works with Rexxar to recruit strong help for the ongoing problems, and his greeting shows little patience for idle conversation.

Borgrim Stouthammer represents the Explorers' League; he says he and Bronwyn are studying the Blade's Edge Mountains for the Alliance, though they came after an extended stay in Silithus for a vacation. He seeks Bloodmaul brew, then turns it into a scheme against their Bladespire enemies. His response mocks the ogres and jokes that they will drink anything.
Station Bot-Jock is a humanoid in the Blade's Edge Mountains.

Commander Skyshadow speaks for Sylvanaar and calls on visitors to contribute to its well-being, warning that surrounding forces threaten the settlement. She regrets driving Toshley and the other gnomes away after their technology disrupted work in the grove, but says they had no choice. She also sees no path to peace with the ogres threatening the area.
Crystal Flayers in Singing Ridge scratch at the singing crystals, disrupting a researcher’s study of their harmonics. This Crystal Flayer is among the creatures the researcher wants cleared away.

Bronwyn Stouthammer is an Explorers' League researcher newly arrived in Blade's Edge with Borgrim. After working in Silithus, she is eager to explore these mountains and study their natural riches. Draenethyst crystals especially intrigue her: she asks for specimens so she can examine them with her tools.
A Rock Flayer target in Blade's Edge Mountains.
An invisible stalker in Blade's Edge Mountains.
This Bloodmaul Drudger is a hostile fighter who greets opponents with crude threats and boasts of smashing them. Its blunt, simple taunts give it a rough, forceful manner in combat.
Dullgrom Dredger is a hostile humanoid combatant whose fighting grows more frenzied when badly wounded.

Vindicator Vuuleen is a captive at Bladespire Hold by choice, using her position to gather information on the Bladespire for Sylvanaar. She says she can leave whenever she wants, but seeks the return of her sword and shield, taken by Droggam and Mugdorg. She asks for help weakening the ogres and disrupting their leaders, and wants the Bladespire banner used to draw Bloodmaul attacks away from Sylvanaar. Her work combines intelligence gathering with protecting the settlement.
A Bladespire ogre champion in the Bladespire Hold area, this fighter greets opponents with threats to smash them. Its short, broken speech presents it as blunt and aggressive.

Fel Corrupters are among the forces spreading corruption across Bladed Gulch, where the Burning Legion's forces threaten local creatures. They are targets in efforts to stop that damage. This Fel Corrupter appears in the gulch and casts a spell while out of combat.

Rokgah Bloodgrip is a Thunderlord artifact seeker in Outland, driven by a long search for the clan's lost relics. He dismisses the Thunderlords as weak for accepting demonic power, yet has studied their texts closely. After the player succeeds where others failed, Rokgah uses a fragment of his own soul to create a vision guide, then sends the player after the Thunderspike because the mine is too deep in Bloodmaul territory for him to enter. He is impressed by the player's success but tempers praise with teasing insults, and says he will return the artifacts to appease the ghosts of Thunderlord Stronghold.
Raven's Wood Stonebark is an elemental fighter.
A Raven’s Wood Leafbeard appears grateful when freed from the koi-koi spirit’s influence.

T'chali is a troll witch doctor who taught the Bloodmaul to brew. After they buried him and left him to die, he seeks revenge on Grimnok and Korgaah and wants his stolen hookah back. He devised a brew intended to strengthen the Bloodmaul and weaken their Bladespire enemies, though he was unsure it would work.
Greater Crust Burster is a burster that stops moving when aggroed.
A Young Crust Burster casts a spell when it enters combat.
A Wyrmcult zealot addresses an overseer, asks whether the attack is ready, and relays that Kolphis Darkscale is looking for them.
A Wyrmcult acolyte addresses an overseer and offers help, with the same greetings also asking whether anything is needed and reporting that Kolphis Darkscale is looking for them.
A Wyrmcult Blackwhelp is a young dragonkin encountered in the Ruuan Weald.
Maxnar the Ashmaw bears the title Wyrmcult Patriarch and is encountered in the Ruuan Weald. In combat he uses Flame Breath, Cleave, and Mortal Strike.
The Cannon Channeler is a one-off support presence at the cannon site.

Gnome Cannon Shooter #1 is a gnome gunner assigned to the cannon operation in Blade's Edge. Its name marks it as one of the numbered shooters, a practical crew role rather than a separately named character.
The Gore-Scythe Ravager is a beast found in two Blade's Edge areas. It is hostile and uses a special attack in combat, fitting the role of dangerous local wildlife.
Station Sharpshooter is a humanoid marksman whose combat routine uses a tech gun.

Tally Zapnabber is an engineer at Toshley's Station who experiments with unusual Outland power sources, especially the Zephyrium Capacitorium. He recruits test subjects for hazardous flights, offers hazard pay, and asks them to sign a waiver while trying to reassure them. Tally says he has improved the device's efficiency and calls Rally his twin, directing subjects to Rally for launch preparations. His confidence gives way to astonishment when test subjects return unharmed.

Rally Zapnabber, Tally's twin, runs the Zephyrium Capacitorium launch service in Blade's Edge Mountains. Travelers can ask him to prepare test flights to Singing Ridge, Razaan's Landing, or Ruuan Weald. His gossip recognizes the resemblance to his twin, and repeat launches can leave travelers temporarily charged.

Daranelle is an investigator studying the Lashh'an arakkoa's magic in Veil Lashh. She asks for help examining their feather-based spellwork because she cannot get close enough herself. After the spell is cast on the visitor, she studies its effects and finds it resembles communion or communication; she is intrigued but still unsure what it means.
Wyrmcult Blessed is a dragonkin combatant whose routine includes casting a spell in combat.

Smiles O'Byron is an engineer at Toshley's Station. He says he built its gnomish transporter with Engineer Lapforge of Gadgetzan, trusts the device while recommending a parachute cloak as a precaution, and discusses the engineering behind personal transport beacons.

Dertrok is a researcher in the village who understands Vekh'nir rituals and is investigating the arakkoa's new activity. He has fashioned four experimental wands to test against the ogre slaves, then directs the findings toward the Cenarion Expedition's Timeon.
Blackscale is a formidable combatant whose attacks include Flame Breath and a terrifying roar.
Death's Watch are a humanoid enemy group in Blade's Edge, named among the forces carrying fel cannon ammunition at Death's Door. They use one attack when first engaged and another during combat.
Death's Might is a creature found across several areas of Blade's Edge Mountains.
A Wyrmcult Scout who addresses an overseer as a subordinate, the scout offers reports and asks whether an attack is ready. The scout says Kolphis Darkscale has been looking for the overseer.
Trogma is a named creature found at Trogma's Claim in Blade's Edge Mountains.
Floaty Flavor Eye is a named creature found in Blade's Edge Mountains.

R-3D0 is Toshley's Station's remote sentry, an autonomous warning construct whose speech is formal, loud and deliberately misleading about the station. It recognizes Sylvanaar and Commander Skyshadow, threatens to play loud sounds, and explains that its gears drown out speech. Its own account of speaking several languages ends by saying it cannot understand the listener.

Toshley takes pride in the station’s experiments and is glad to have left the stuffy elves of Sylvanaar. Eager for cheap energy and obedient electromentals, Toshley sends volunteers to harvest lightning despite a calculated risk of implosion. Discovering gnome souls in Razaani orbs provokes outrage and a demand to stop Nexus-Prince Razaan.
Cansis is a humanoid in the Blade's Edge Mountains.
A small electromental.

Nickwinkle the Metro-Gnome is a scientist studying time and sound. He investigates the singing crystals, their possible relationship with nether drakes, and the arakkoa, while the noise around his research site irritates him. He has a playful vanity about his appearance and an eccentric collection of odds and ends.
Big Electromental Flavor is an elemental found in the Blades Edge Mountains and Borean Tundra.

Timeon is a Cenarion Expedition researcher investigating the arakkoa and the Raven cult. He is troubled by the cult's growing influence and wants to understand its teachings and the nature of the Raven. His interests differ markedly from Dertrok's, though they have discussed the arakkoa.
A wyrm known as Wyrm from Beyond, found in the Blade’s Edge Mountains.

A Wyrmcult poacher in the Blade’s Edge Mountains, associated with the cult’s presence across several local areas. It calls a Wyrmcult Broodling while out of combat, linking its field role to the cult’s broodlings.
Wyrmcult Hewers are tree cutters whose destruction of the Ruuan Weald brings them into conflict with defenders of the forest.

Dizzy Dina is one of Razak’s Roughriders, helping protect Toshley’s operation in Outland. She sends help against stalkers and gathers material for the scientists’ research, though she is plainly disgusted by handling the flesh herself. Her rough humor shows in the stink joke, and she values persistence: she says a Roughrider follows orders and fights until death.

Taerek is a quest giver in the village who needs silkwing cocoons for its uses there. He says the village's warriors are occupied defending it, and notes that experiments raising silkwing larvae have not yielded enough silk.
Silmara asks for iridescent silkwing wings, explaining that the village uses them in many ways, including as decorative inlays. She says they will put the wings to use soon.
A gnome cannon shooter associated with Shattrath.
A gnome cannon shooter associated with Singing Ridge.
A gnome cannon shooter associated with Ruuan.

Garm Wolfbrother is the Thunderlord Clan's chieftain and readily offers advice against the ogres. Knowing Rexxar seeks his people, Garm wants him told where the Mok'Nathal village lies and that its people are in danger.
A Thunderlord Clan sub-chief with a subordinate leadership role among the clan.
Lobo is a named beast.
Rema is known as the den mother and primary defender of the Jagged Ridge south of Thunderlord Stronghold. She keeps to a tunnel at the ridge's southern edge.
A sober member of the Bladespire defenders, this elite combatant serves among the guards in the Bladespire area.

Overseer Nuaar leads the wyrmcultists in the Ruuan Weald. He resents the Cenarion Expedition's objections to exploiting the region, asking who they are to dictate how others take advantage of its opportunities.

Samia Inkling is Baron Sablemane's expert on the wyrmcult, sent to help the Cenarion Expedition. Curious and methodical, she studies the Blackwing Coven and wants live blackwhelps to understand what the cult reveres and what the druids face. She appreciates the poachers' nets for their craftsmanship, even as she calls their skill misdirected.

Rexxar, Champion of the Horde, feels the weight of finding and defending the Mok'Nathal alongside the Horde's conflicts. Having left his people to follow the Horde to Azeroth, he longs for his father Leoroxx's acceptance and wants to grow stronger before facing him. He seeks the motives behind ogre attacks, relying on his hawk Spirit for covert scouting. His bond with his wyvern Leokk drives him to seek the captive creature's release.

Leoroxx is a Mok'Nathal who judges outsiders by what they can do. He describes his people as struggling to survive among their enemies and wants a better life for them. He tests a visitor's prowess against threats to the Mok'Nathal, including the Bladespire ogres and Vekh'nir, and treats success as only a first step toward understanding his people.

Tree Warden Chawn works to restore nature's balance in the Ruuan Weald and protect its trees and wildlife. He first supports negotiation with the Wyrmcult, but turns to force when they reject compromise and keep damaging the forest. He is defiant toward the Blackwing Coven and regards stopping its leader as protection for the region; he also worries over unnatural forces affecting the natural world.

Kolphis Darkscale is a named figure at the Blackwing Coven, where an undercover visitor posing as Overseer Nuaar can speak with him. A note dropped by a cultist bears Kolphis’s signature. When he mistakes the disguised visitor for Nuaar, he orders them to carry out their orders at Ruuan Weald.

O’Mally Zapnabber, “Tally’s Other Twin,” is an inquisitive researcher and practical fixer. He studies the druids’ power and measures druid magic, while testing weather instruments. He also recognizes a damaged mask as a Legion communication device and repairs it, showing his interest in how unfamiliar devices work.
A bat target in Blade's Edge Mountains.
A cave bat found in Outland.

A cavern crawler is a hostile beast found in Outland’s Blade’s Edge region. It fights with a spell when wounded, and crawlers in the area are targets in the effort to clear the tunnels for trade with the Harborage.
A cave bat found in Outland.
Daggermaw Blackhides are beasts found across several areas of Outland’s Blade’s Edge region. They fight with a combat spell.

Mosswood the Ancient is the last survivor of a people driven from their wood when the Burning Legion sent imps to burn it centuries ago. His lost home lies near Skald. He preserved ironroot seeds in hope of restoring the wood, and still hungers for revenge on the scorched imps, though he knows they cannot all be destroyed. The effort has given him hope of trying to revive his beloved wood for a few more centuries.

npcs.name: Air Force Guard Post (Toshley's Station - Flying Machine)

records.text: A mechanical Air Force guard post in flying-machine form, associated with Toshley's Station.
A Wyrmcult provisioner who recognizes an overseer reassigned to Ruuan Weald, welcomes their return, and offers wares with an easy familiarity.

A friend of Rexxar who believes even friendship must carry a price, Baron Sablemane is driven by hatred of Gruul and his sons. He recruits help against the Bladespire ogres and plans to join the fight against their master, Goc.
A blackwhelp of the brood raised by the Wyrmcult at Blackwing Coven, sought alive for examination.
A beast named Tethik.

Wildlord Antelarion enjoys walking and stretching all four limbs. Antelarion coordinates deception of the Burning Legion using duplicated Felsworn masks and a false revolt report, and sends allies to investigate Death’s Door with a druid signal. Antelarion can sharply call helpers expendable while demanding action against Doomcryer, yet offers lavish gratitude for success.
A black dragon whelp associated with Baron Sablemane.
A mature cavern crawler found in the local caverns. In combat, it casts a spell.

Faradrella is a draenei who asks for help stopping the Burning Legion’s corruption of the local creatures. She directs the player toward Bladed Gulch to confront the Fel Corrupters and Felsworn, and says the destruction is regrettable but necessary to halt the corruption.
A tame clefthoof found in the local area.
Dubu is a creature found in the local area.
A quilbeast found in the local area.
Zakk is a creature found in the local area.

Commander Haephus Stonewall represents Sylvanaar’s interests in Ruuan Weald and is concerned about Horde travel through the area. He investigates the Bloodmaul ogres’ planned attacks on Sylvanaar and Ruuan Weald, identifies Gorgrom as their hidden instigator, and seeks Baron Sablemane’s help to make a trap for the gronn. His response to the ogres is forceful: he calls for their leaders to be killed and for Gorgrom’s defeat to send them a warning.

Lieutenant Fairweather is a Sylvanaar representative in Ruuan Weald who urges direct action against the mountain ogres. She assigns attacks on Bloodmaul at the camp and Bladespire at Boulder'mok, and sees each ogre killed as a step toward removing a danger that will not leave the region in peace. Her praise for the player’s fighting is enthusiastic; she says she wishes she could have joined the battle and warns against duties that keep her from the battlefield.
A Bloodmaul Taskmaster is a hostile ogre who threatens attackers in blunt, broken phrases, repeatedly boasting that he will smash them. His taunts show a combative, aggressive manner.
Trigul is a named, unusually powerful creature encountered alone. It uses two different abilities.
An Apexis Flayer is a hostile creature that attacks with Rend and Shred Armor.
The Shard-Hide Boar is a boar that responds to combat with Spell Reflection.
Aether Rays are creatures that can appear ready to be wrangled. They also defend themselves in combat with a tail swipe.
The Lightning Wasp is a hostile creature that attacks with a lightning-themed ability when combat begins.
Bladespine Basilisks are beasts that cast a spell when combat begins.
Wrath Speakers are demons that fight with Rain of Chaos and Curse of Weakness, and respond to Banishment.
Wrath Reavers are elite mechanical foes that cast a spell as they fight.
Nightmare Imps are demons found in the area.
Fear Fiends are demons that react to Banishment.
An Expedition Druid is an elite druid of the Expedition, encountered in the field.

Treebole is an ancient of lore, a leafbeard whose boughs shelter birds that bring him news. He works to free the Raven's Wood trees from possession and says he keeps magic rings for heroes who help the woods.
Fhyn Leafshadow serves as a flight master, offering air travel to visitors. When attacked, he summons an enraged gryphon and an enraged wyvern.
A Felstorm Corruptor is a hostile combatant that casts spells when engaged and during combat.
An Insidious Familiar is a hostile demon that uses a spell in combat.
A Felstorm Overseer is a hostile demon that casts spells in combat, including one as its health falls.
A Grishna arakkoa of Grishnath. The arakkoa's language is normally indecipherable to outsiders; their souls can be used to understand it briefly, helping investigators seek the Raven's prophecy.
An unsuspecting Leafbeard of Raven's Wood, a tree folk threatened when Grishna magic fills the local leafbeards with evil koi-koi spirits.
An evil koi-koi spirit inhabiting the leafbeards of Raven's Wood. Exorcism feathers made from a Grishnath orb and dire pinfeather can draw out and slay these spirits.
A Bash'ir raider encountered among the Bash'ir in Netherstorm. In combat, this raider uses Energy Flare and Warp.
A Bash'ir spell-thief encountered among the Bash'ir in Netherstorm.
A Bash'ir arcanist encountered among the Bash'ir in Netherstorm.
An unbound ethereal is a hostile creature that casts a spell.
A hostile Wrath Corruptor casts Shadow Bolt and Corruption in combat, adjusts its movement as foes approach or its mana runs low, and flees for assistance when critically wounded.
The Ogri'la Steelshaper sells blacksmithing supplies and speaks of steel as trustworthy, saying its strength comes from the one who wields it. Its greeting addresses the listener as “exalted one.”
The Ogri'la Grubgiver sells food and hopes it satisfies visitors, even the mightiest of hungers. It addresses visitors as mighty one.
Leokk is a named wyvern captured by Bladespire ogres and held in a cage. A key and Spirit's Whistle are part of a plan to free him.
The Ogri'la Merchant sells general goods and welcomes visitors as friends, asking what they would like to see.
An Ogri’la trade-goods merchant who offers service with a respectful greeting of “exalted one.”
A Witness of Doom that uses Stealth Detection.
An eredar stormbringer demon.
A Fel Rager elemental.
A Darkflame infernal demon.
A guard stationed among the demonic forces around the furnace, this creature fights intruders and contributes to the “Banish the Demons” effort when slain.
A Vile Fire-Soul is a fire elemental encountered among hostile forces around the furnace. It casts a spell in combat.

Vekh leads the Vekh’nir arakkoa, who have enslaved ogres in Trogma’s Claim. Leoroxx identifies him as their leader and calls for him to be slain as part of the Mok’Nathal’s struggle for survival. In battle, Vekh can heal when wounded and uses Whirlwind.
A small cavern crawler found in the caverns of Outland.
A Wyrmcult hunter encountered among the cult’s forces. It casts a spell in combat.

Spiritcaller Dohgar is a Mok'Nathal spiritcaller who honors ancestral spirits and wants them treated with respect. He condemns the Bladespire ogres' use of totems to control, and sees taking those totems as a way to put them to respectful use. He also seeks to free nether drake spirits and investigate the Razaani's pink light orbs, which remind him of souls. He praises those who act on behalf of the Mok'Nathal and calls the ethereals' leader and followers filth.
A Terror-Fire Guardian in the Blade's Edge Mountains, it is a demon that can be banished.
A Bloodmaul Soothsayer is a hulking, aggressive combatant whose taunts promise smashing and crushing opponents. It casts Demon Armor when it respawns.
Terrordar the Tormentor is a solitary elite in Blade’s Edge Mountains. In combat, he uses two distinct offensive abilities.

Watcher Moonshade leads the defense at Wyrmskull Tunnel, where he expects a stand against the massing wyrmcultists. He asks whether Draaca Longtail is dead and aims to sow confusion among their ranks, though he warns an overseer could replace her. He also asks about news from Evergrove.
The Wrath Fiend is a demon found in Blade’s Edge Mountains.

Draaca Longtail is a wyrmcultist leader in Wyrmskull Tunnel. Watcher Moonshade believes removing her could prompt a struggle over leadership and ease the pressure, while warning that an overseer might take her place. In combat, Draaca can frenzy and use Cutdown.

An Expedition Outrider stationed in Blade’s Edge Mountains. The supplied records identify the outrider and its expedition affiliation, but give no individual biography or specific duty beyond the role in its name.

An Evergrove druid who warns that the Burning Legion is increasing its use of Death’s Door to summon fel hounds and other creatures. The druid urges action against the portal and explains that fel cannon ammunition can be imbued with nature’s force to threaten the Legion and its creations.
Sky-Master Maxxor arranges air travel as a flight master and can summon enraged wyverns when attacked.
Natasha is a humanoid in the Blade's Edge Mountains.
Ogrin is a stable master offering pet stabling and help recovering lost companions.
Fiskal Shadowsong is a stable master offering pet stabling and help recovering lost companions.
A beast bearing the name Death's Door North Warp-Gate in Blade's Edge Mountains.
A beast bearing the name Death's Door South Warp-Gate in Blade's Edge Mountains.
Brown Marmot is a critter found in the Zangarmarsh area.

Sentinel Moonwhisper is a sentinel at a tunnel post. The assigned task asks adventurers to clear the Cavern Crawlers so trade with the Harborage can proceed; Moonwhisper says they must remain at their post and sends the report to Commander Skyshadow.

Grunt Grahk is a grunt at a tunnel post. Grahk asks adventurers to clear the Cavern Crawlers so trade with Swamp Rat can proceed, says they must remain at their post, and directs the report to Tor'chunk Twoclaws.
Second Prophecy is one of four shrines at Grishnath bearing messages from the Oracles of the Raven. Their totems let the arakkoa hear the Word of the Raven; this is the second prophecy.
Third Prophecy is one of four shrines at Grishnath bearing messages from the Oracles of the Raven. Their totems let the arakkoa hear the Word of the Raven; this is the third prophecy.
Fourth Prophecy is one of four shrines at Grishnath bearing messages from the Oracles of the Raven. Their totems let the arakkoa hear the Word of the Raven; this is the fourth prophecy.

Vim'gol the Vile is an ogre warlock who trained Skulloc Soulgrinder. He is summoned at his circle in the mountains northeast of the Broken Wilds, challenges those who call him, and threatens to grow bigger and crush them. His vile grimoire is sought by adventurers.

Image of Commander Ameer speaks for the Protectorate about the Ethereum's stasis prisons. He concludes they hold ferocious beasts and creatures from many worlds that the Ethereum hope to command, and urges their destruction. He presses the effort toward the Mana-Tombs, seeking a Mark of the Nexus-King to make a key, and shudders at the horrors expected in the final prisons.
An Ethereum prisoner held in Stasis Chamber Alpha in Blade's Edge Mountains.
Innkeeper Aelerya is individually identified as an innkeeper. Her greeting welcomes weary travelers and asks what she can do for them; visitors can make the inn their home.

Arthorn Windsong is a Cenarion researcher at the Evergrove who has studied Blade’s Edge arakkoa with Timeon. She is eager to uncover the raven cult’s history and interprets the recovered text as evidence that Anzu threatens the Emerald Dream. Arthorn hopes her work will persuade Morthis Whisperwing to take her as a student, and she has worked with Watcher Elaira on trained sparrowhawks that carry messages.

Sai’kkal the Elder is an arakkoa ghost sought out for information about the Book of the Raven. In an encounter, he reaches toward a visitor as if trying to identify them, says he cannot see clearly, and asks whether they are Rokkaram.

Mog'dorg is a Bloodmaul ogre working to free his clan from the Sons of Gruul and Gruul's backing of the Bladespire clan. He seeks a home where ogres can choose their own fate, and hopes the crystal in the staff gifted by Ogri'la can let him share his clear speech with his kin.

Chort stands at the tower above the Circle of Blood, where Mog'dorg directs visitors to meet him. He urges visitors to keep quiet about what they see and hear, and says he is ready to serve the new king or queen.

The Bladespire Supplicant speaks as a deferential follower of the player, professing a life for them and imagining a new king leading ogres to Ogri'la after Gruul's sons are gone. Other conditional lines mix anxious questions with jokes about dancing and a kiss.
A Legion flak cannon stationed in Blade's Edge.
The Ogri'la Keg King is a drink vendor who jokes that cocktails are the group's secret diet and offers to help visitors with one.
Mingo is an Ogri'la reagent vendor whose greetings range from a helpful offer to a warm, sibling-like address for an exalted visitor.
One of Ogri'la's peacekeepers, stationed among the settlement's guards.

A bombing-run target used by the Skyguard against the fel cannonball stacks threatening Ogri’la. Skyguard bombs trigger its quest-credit response; it serves as a target for the bombing exercise rather than a speaking character.

Sky Sergeant Vanderlip is a Skyguard sergeant who warns rookies about the dangers of flying over the Blade’s Edge Mountains and urges them to keep working against the demons. Vanderlip directs bombing runs against fel cannonball stacks threatening Ogri’la, praises successful work, and jokes about Old Man Keller doubting the recruit. The replies also frame pilot rest as enforced policy.
The Skyguard Pyrotechnician is a field-supplies vendor. Its brief greeting offers supplies.

Chu'a'lor is a two-headed ogre who speaks for Ogri'la, the crystal-enhanced community seeking peace in its mountain home. He studies the Apexis relics and values the insight gained in learning to use them. He welcomes the freed ogres' efforts to reunite their clans, directs newcomers toward Mog'dorg's resistance, and regards the Skyguard as allies in protecting Ogri'la. His thanks to those who help carry both gratitude and a reminder that their work also protects the ogres below.

Kronk is an Ogri’la ogre who says past violence has been left behind. Confident in years of crystal lore and demon study, Kronk seeks to protect Ogri’la and the Skyguard through banishment. Darkrune creation remains unreliable, and Kronk can hardly bear to inspect the results. Visitors are asked to take it easy on newcomer Gahk.
A storyteller associated with Ogri’la.

Agadai is an apprentice wind rider master who cares for the beasts between flights. With too few mounts and almost no downtime, Agadai fears they will be worked to death and asks Dama Wildmane, who oversees care and training at Shadowmoon Village, for replacements.

Gahk is a two-headed ogre of Ogri'la whose heads nod to each other. Crystal-making has made him smarter and gives him headaches, though he says he would rather smash demons than think. He wants to use darkrunes and demon chiefs' whips against demons threatening Ogri'la.

Torkus is a two-headed father with ten sons. Since coming to Ogri'la, crystal exposure has made the family more aware and left them with headaches; the sons now pester him about joining the Sha'tari Skyguard. He is trying to help them pursue that ambition and speaks with weary paternal concern.

Sky Commander Keller leads the Skyguard Outpost and claims to have built it with his own hands. Blunt about the dangers of service, he welcomes recruits as “fresh meat” and sends them to sharp-tongued Sergeant Vanderlip. He regards the dragons as fierce predators threatening safe flight. Keller also calls the aether-techs' trips to Bash'ir Landing assaults, despite their talk of study, and sees the crystalforge as a source of supplies and goods to sell.

Skyguard Khatie is an engaging, flirtatious member of the Sha'tari Skyguard who organizes efforts to secure aether rays as mounts. She explains that bombing runs and missions to Bash'ir Landing have depleted the Skyguard's mounts, and connects replacing them with helping protect Ogri'la. Her banter grows more familiar as the player's standing with the Skyguard rises: she hints at spending time together, jokes about being a lowly peon beside the player's fame, and expresses that she misses the player. She also appreciates rays brought back to her, while noting that returning them was not necessary.
Tork is a humanoid found in the Blade's Edge Mountains.
Torki is a humanoid found in the Blade's Edge Mountains.
A Gan’arg Analyzer is a demon.
The Skyguard Stable Master handles pet stabling and help recovering lost companions. Their greeting presents both as services for Skyguard visitors.

Skyguard handler Irena offers a direct flight to the faction’s base at Blackwind Landing, contingent on getting in good with the Skyguard. She warmly calls travelers “comrade” and proudly points out her beautiful nether ray.

Jho’nass is Ogri’la’s trusted quartermaster, stocking goods made by the ogres and special brews for sale to the group’s appreciated guests. His greetings are relaxed and welcoming; he treats a visitor’s interest in the store with easygoing enthusiasm.

The Aether-tech Apprentice helps coordinate the Skyguard’s missions to Bash’ir Landing. In response to the claim that these are assaults, the apprentice prefers to call them research, while acknowledging that the team also resupplies the Skyguard and sells surplus crystalforge goods when able.

The Blade’s Edge Flame Warden tends the Alliance festival flame in Blade’s Edge Mountains. In the Midsummer greeting, the warden welcomes Alliance visitors, urges them to honor Alliance fires across Azeroth, and condemns Horde fires, encouraging their desecration. The greeting is conditional; it does not establish when the warden is available.

The Blade’s Edge Flame Keeper tends the Horde festival flame in Blade’s Edge Mountains. The keeper welcomes Horde visitors, urges them to honor Horde fires across Azeroth, and condemns Alliance fires, encouraging their desecration.
Frixee Brasstumbler is an Arena Vendor in Blade’s Edge Mountains. Her vendor service lets visitors browse her goods.

place_records.text: You are in Blade's Edge Mountains, contested land in Outland where both the Alliance and the Horde hold settlements. The Horde keeps Thunderlord Stronghold and Mok'Nathal Village, while the Alliance holds Sylvanaar, Toshley's Station and Evergrove. Bladespire and Bloodmaul ogre clans fight over the ravines and ridges between these camps, so the mountains stay dangerous.

You are in Blades' Run, a Horde tunnel post in Blade's Edge Mountains. Grunt Grahk keeps the post and wants the Cavern Crawlers in the tunnel cleared so that trade with Swamp Rat can flow. Cavern Crawlers still infest the passage.

You are in Jagged Ridge, where Rema, the den mother, defends the southern edge from a tunnel. Thunderlord dire wolves are found here, and Bladewing bloodletters roam the ridge. The Alliance remote sentry R-3D0 gives loud, deliberately misleading warnings about Toshley's Station.

You are in Thunderlord Stronghold, a Horde fortress in Blade's Edge Mountains that the Horde recently took back from ogres. Chieftain Garm Wolfbrother leads the Thunderlord clan here, and Tor'chunk Twoclaws urges attacks on the nearby ogre clans. Gor'drek directs efforts against bloodletters and Alliance defenses. Its inn and wind rider master, Unoke Tenderhoof, serve visitors.

You are in The Living Grove, an Alliance grove beside Sylvanaar in Blade's Edge Mountains. Rina Moonspring tends it, using a nature-imbued bough to call treant defenders. Fey drakes pollinate the grove. Grovestalker lynxes have slipped out of control and now encroach on Sylvanaar.

You are in Sylvanaar, an Alliance settlement in Blade's Edge Mountains. Commander Skyshadow speaks for it and warns that surrounding forces threaten it. Borgrim and Bronwyn Stouthammer of the Explorers' League are studying the mountains, and Daranelle studies arakkoa magic in Veil Lashh. Visitors find an inn and a hippogryph master.

You are in Bladespire Hold, where Bladespire ogres keep their brutes, shamans and raptors. Vindicator Vuuleen is a captive here by choice, gathering information for Sylvanaar. She wants her sword and shield back from the Bladespire leaders who took them.

You are in Gruul's Lair, a lair where Bladespire ogres keep a captive wyvern, Leokk, in a cage. Bladespire enforcers, ravagers and battlemages guard it, and a key and Spirit's Whistle are part of a plan to free him.

You are in Circle of Blood, a neutral arena in Blade's Edge Mountains run by the Steamwheedle Fighting Circuit, where Steamwheedle Sam organizes bouts and Lefty Puddemup is the arena battlemaster. Baron Sablemane recruits help against the Bladespire ogres, and Mog'dorg the Wizened, a Bloodmaul ogre, seeks a home where ogres choose their own fate.

You are in Bloodmaul Outpost, an ogre outpost in Blade's Edge Mountains. Bloodmaul skirmishers, geomancers, brutes and dire wolves hold it, and Bloodmaul brewmasters keep barrels of brutebane brew here.
You are in Bloodmaul Camp, an ogre camp in Blade's Edge Mountains. Bloodmaul maulers and warlocks gather here, with battle worgs at their side, and Speaker Mar'grom is among its ogres.
You are in Trogma's Claim, in Blade's Edge Mountains, where Vekh'nir stormcallers and dreadhawks hunt alongside Dullgrom dredgers. Trogma is among the foes here.
You are in Blackwing Coven, in Blade's Edge Mountains, where the Wyrmcult raises its brood of blackwhelps. Wyrmcult scouts, zealots and acolytes lurk here, and a blackscale is among the threats.

You are in Grishnath, a neutral ground in the Blade's Edge Mountains that neither side holds. A spirit healer here offers a return to the living for a price, and four prophecy shrines carry the Oracles of the Raven's messages to the arakkoa. Treebole, an ancient of lore, works to free the Raven's Wood trees from possession, while Grishna harbingers and basilisks roam the ground and dire ravens use a spell when wounded.

You are in Veil Lashh, a part of the Blade's Edge Mountains where the Alliance keeps a small presence. Lashh'an windwalkers, wing guards and talonites roam here, and a Lashh'an matriarch is among them, while Lashh'an spell circles stand here with pictograms that remain confusing to those who read them. Stronglimb Deeproot, an ancient of war, is chief defender of the Living Grove south of Sylvanaar.

You are in Veil Vekh, a stretch of the Blade's Edge Mountains that neither side keeps. Vekh'nir keeneyes, dreadhawks and stormcallers haunt the ground, a Vekh'nir matriarch among them, and arakkoa eggs lie about. Silkwing larvae change form as they are wounded.

You are in Forge Camp: Terror, a camp of the Legion in the Blade's Edge Mountains. Abyssal flamebringers, nightmare imps and fear fiends fill its ground, along with terror-fire guardians and vile fire-souls. Legion fel cannons stand here among them.

You are in Forge Camp: Wrath, a camp of the Legion in the Blade's Edge Mountains. Wrath hounds, fel ragers and furnace guards roam it, and wrath speakers and wyrmcult blackwhelps are found here too. Legion flak cannons are set up in the camp as well.

You are in Ogri'la, a crystal-enhanced community of ogres in the Blade's Edge Mountains that seeks peace. Chu'a'lor, a two-headed ogre, speaks for it and studies the Apexis relics, while Torkus, a two-headed father, has ten sons who pester him to join the Sha'tari Skyguard. Its merchants sell smithing supplies, food, goods and drinks, but ogres down below remain enslaved by the Sons of Gruul.

You are in Forge Camp: Anger, a camp of the Legion in the Blade's Edge Mountains. Anger guards, doomforge attendants and doomforge engineers hold its ground, with legion fel cannons among them. The camp has reportedly revolted against its commander.

You are in Bloodmaul Ravine, a place in the Blade's Edge Mountains where the Horde keeps a presence. T'chali the Witch Doctor, a troll who taught the Bloodmaul to brew, was buried here by the Bloodmaul and still wants his hookah back and revenge on Grimnok and Korgaah. Bloodmaul skirmishers, brutes, geomancers and brewmasters roam the ravine, with dire wolves among them.

You are in Daggermaw Canyon, neutral ground in the Blade's Edge Mountains where Expedition wardens and outriders keep order. Bloodmaul maulers, warlocks, taskmasters and soothsayers roam it. A black dragon whelp associated with Baron Sablemane is found here as well.

You are in Vekhaar Stand, a stretch of the Blade's Edge Mountains that neither side keeps. Mature and cosmetic silkwings fill the ground, with Vekh'nir stormcallers and dreadhawks among them. Dullgrom dredgers and Deathforge technicians are found here too, and silkwing larvae change form as they are wounded.

You are in Ruuan Weald, a part of the Blade's Edge Mountains where neither side keeps a settlement. Wyrmcult poachers and hewers roam its ground under Overseer Nuaar, who leads the wyrmcultists here and resents the Cenarion Expedition's objections to exploiting the region. Ruuan'ok skyfuries are dangerous, and outraged Raven's Wood saplings use a spell as their health falls.

You are in Veil Ruuan, a stretch of the Blade's Edge Mountains that neither side keeps. Ruuan'ok ravenguards, cloudgazers and skyfuries prowl it, along with a Ruuan Weald basilisk, wyrmcult poachers and arakkoa eggs.

You are in Raven's Wood, an area of Blade's Edge Mountains in Outland. Outraged Raven's Wood Saplings are hostile plant creatures here that use a spell as their health falls. Dire Ravens are dangerous wild birds that also use a spell when badly wounded. Wyrmcult Scouts and Raven's Wood Stonebarks are hostile here too.

You are in Death's Door, a place in Blade's Edge Mountains in Outland where the Burning Legion has a portal. An Evergrove druid warns that the Legion uses it to summon fel hounds and other creatures. Baelmon the Hound-Master maintains the ritual that keeps the portal working, and Death's Might and Deathforge technicians fight here.

You are in Vortex Pinnacle, an area of Blade's Edge Mountains in Outland. Its spirit healer offers a return to life for a price. Sai'kkal the Elder, an arakkoa ghost, is sought out for information about the Book of the Raven, and he says he cannot see clearly. Gan'arg Analyzers and Wrath Corruptors are hostile here.

You are in Razor Ridge, an area of Blade's Edge Mountains in Outland. A profession trainer is among its services. Rip-Blade Ravagers, Gore-Scythe Ravagers and Daggermaw Lashtails are hostile here, along with Ridgespine Stalkers and Scalewing Serpents. Gnome cannon shooters work the cannon operation in Blade's Edge.

You are in Mok'Nathal Village, a Horde settlement in Blade's Edge Mountains in Outland. It has an inn, a flight master and vendors, and Matron Varah keeps the inn. Spiritcaller Dohgar honors ancestral spirits and condemns the Bladespire ogres' use of totems, while Dertrok researches the arakkoa's new rituals. Mature Silkwings are hostile here.
You are in Churning Gulch, a gulch in Blade's Edge Mountains in Outland. Young and greater Crust Bursters are the main dangers here, along with Daggermaw Blackhides.

You are in Bash'ir Landing, an area of Blade's Edge Mountains in Outland where Commander Ameer speaks for the Protectorate. His image says the Ethereum's stasis prisons hold ferocious beasts and urges their destruction. Ethereum prisoners are held in stasis chambers here, and Bash'ir raiders, arcanists and spell-thieves are hostile, along with lightning wasps.

You are in Crystal Spine, an area of Blade's Edge Mountains in Outland. Its spirit healer offers a return to life for a price. Felstorm Corruptors, Darkflame Infernals and Shard-Hide Boars are hostile here, and Legion fel cannons are too. Aether Rays appear ready to be wrangled.
You are in Skald, an area of Blade's Edge Mountains in Outland. Searing Elementals, Scorch Imps and Scalded Basilisks are hostile here, along with Felsworn Daggermaws and Rip-Blade Ravagers.

You are in Bladed Gulch, a gulch in Blade's Edge Mountains in Outland. A spirit healer offers a return to life for a price here. Felsworn Daggermaws and Fel Corrupters are the main dangers, with Felsworn Scalewings and Ridgespine Horrors.
You are in Boulder'mok, an area of Blade's Edge Mountains in Outland. Boulder'mok brutes, shamans and a chieftain are hostile here.

You are in Toshley's Station, an Alliance settlement in Blade's Edge Mountains in Outland. It has an inn, a flight master and repairs, and Toshley takes pride in the station's experiments. Razak Ironsides commands the defenders against ravager attacks from Gore-Scythe and Rip-Blade Ravagers. Tally Zapnabber tests unusual power sources and sends volunteers on hazardous flights.

You are in Singing Ridge, a ridge in Blade's Edge Mountains. Crystal flayers and wyrms from beyond roam it, and a dreadwing hunts above. Lesser nether drakes are found here, and a gnome cannon shooter tied to Ruuan.

You are in Bladespire Outpost, a site in Blade's Edge Mountains. Bladespire crushers and mystics roam it with Death's Watch and Death's Might, and a hostile named Maggoc is among the threats. A small electromental, Mini-Electromental Flavor, is found here too.
You are in Bladespire Grounds, an area of Blade's Edge Mountains. Bladespire brutes, shamans, raptors and champions roam it, along with Daggermaw blackhides and Bloodmaul skirmishers.

You are in Razaan's Landing, a site in Blade's Edge Mountains where Razaani raiders and nexus stalkers roam, along with Deadsoul orb flights. A Razaani light orb, which reacts when struck by Magnetic Pull, and a fiendling flesh beast, whose ether-energized flesh is collected for study, are found here too.

You are in Evergrove, an Alliance settlement in Blade's Edge Mountains with an inn and repairs. Timeon and Arthorn Windsong, both Cenarion researchers, are troubled by the Raven cult's growing influence. Lieutenant Fairweather urges direct action against the mountain ogres, and Wyrmcult poachers and Grishna arakkoa are the dangers around it.

You are in Wyrmskull Bridge, a crossing in Blade's Edge Mountains that leads west toward the Wyrmskull Tunnel. Watcher Moonshade leads the defense at the tunnel, where wyrmcultists are massing under Draaca Longtail, their leader there. Expedition Wardens enforce conduct on the neutral ground here.

You are in Scalewing Shelf, a ledge in Blade's Edge Mountains. Scalewing serpents, Deathforge technicians, Daggermaw lashtails and Ridgespine stalkers roam it, and a Wyrm from Beyond is among them. A spirit healer offers a return to life here, for a price.

You are in Dragonspine Ridge, a ridge in Blade's Edge Mountains where wyrmcultists roam. Wyrmcult hewers, poachers and hunters are among the dangers here, with Draaca Longtail, the cult's leader in Wyrmskull Tunnel, among them. Expedition druids and Expedition Wardens are found here too.

You are in Skyguard Outpost, a Skyguard post in Blade's Edge Mountains, and its stable master keeps pets. Sky Commander Keller leads it. Sky Sergeant Vanderlip directs bombing runs on fel cannonball stacks that threaten Ogri'la, and those runs and missions to Bash'ir Landing have worn down the Skyguard's mounts, so Skyguard Khatie is organizing the capture of aether rays to replace them.

You are in Shartuul's Transporter, a site in Blade's Edge Mountains. Wrath corruptors, Bladespine basilisks and Wrath reavers are its dangers, and aether rays, which swipe with their tails when attacked, are found here too.
